precepts.text: Jeroboam made two calves of gold and said, Behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt; and he set the one in Bethel, and the other put he in Dan, and this thing became a sin. He made priests of the lowest of the people, and ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, devised of his own heart, in place of the feast of tabernacles. That is the shame of Bethel. Images shown in class: the horned gods of Chinese religion, carved with the cow's head and body, very similar to Baal, the calf god. More proof of who they are.
precepts.point: And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel their confidence.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
“And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Beth–el their confidence.” Chemosh was their god; Moab always had a lot of gods, but Chemosh was the favorite. Notice it says the house of Israel, the northern kingdom, was ashamed of Bethel. What is it talking about?

“Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” Two calves, and our people were worshipping them. “And he set the one in Beth–el, and the other put he in Dan. And this thing became a sin: for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan.”

“And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi.” Then “Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah”. Judah kept the feast of tabernacles on the fifteenth day of the seventh month; Jeroboam and the northern kingdom said, we are going to do the eighth month, the fifteenth day, “even in the month which he had devised of his own heart”, sacrificing unto the calves in Bethel. That is the shame of Bethel: calves of gold, false priests and a feast made up in his own heart.

Moab will be ashamed of its gods the same way. Look at the gods in China today: horned gods, very similar to Baal, the calf god, carved in stone with the cow’s head and body. Israel had two calves; these gods have the same horns. More proof of who they are. And just as Israel was brought to shame for Bethel, Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh.

precepts.text: Like as thou hast done unto my chosen, saith the Lord, even so shall God do unto thee. Thy children shall die of hunger, thy cities shall be broken down, and they that be in the mountains shall die of hunger and eat their own flesh: everybody thinks they have a plan for when Armageddon takes place, we will go into the bunkers and survive there; no, that is not going to happen. And in the passage they shall rush on the idle city, and shall destroy some portion of thy land, and shall return to Babylon that was destroyed. Although the country of Babylon the great is wiped out, her military is not finished; that is why America keeps over 800 military bases worldwide, which no other nation has, not Russia, not China. That is how they reach Moab even after the homeland is destroyed. Thy children shall they carry away captive, and look, what thou hast, they shall spoil it, and mar the beauty of thy face.
precepts.point: For thus saith the Lord; Behold, he shall fly as an eagle, and shall spread his wings over Moab. Whose symbol is the eagle? America. The eagle spreads his wings over Moab, and Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
Jeremiah says Moab “shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord.” Ezra shows the same judgment and why it comes: “Like as thou hast done unto my chosen, saith the Lord, even so shall God do unto thee, and shall deliver thee into mischief”. It goes into what they did to us. What was done to the chosen will be done back to them.

Remember who the subject is. Back in verse 46: “And thou, Asia, that art partaker of the hope of Babylon, and art the glory of her person”. This is Asia, East Asia in particular, the same Moab of Jeremiah 48 that burns incense to all kinds of gods and ancestors.

“Thy children shall die of hunger, and thou shalt fall through the sword: thy cities shall be broken down, and all thine shall perish with the sword in the field. They that be in the mountains shall die of hunger, and eat their own flesh, and drink their own blood”. That is cannibalism. They that be in the mountains are the ones in those bunkers, little bunkers, big bunkers, all kinds of bunkers. Everybody thinks they have a plan for when Armageddon takes place and all nations fight: we will go into the bunkers, we will survive there, we will live there for a century. No, that is not going to happen.

“And in the passage they shall rush on the idle city, and shall destroy some portion of thy land, and consume part of thy glory, and shall return to Babylon that was destroyed.” The idle city is China. And it shows America is not finished yet. Although the country, Babylon the great, the United States of America, gets wiped out, her military is not finished. That is why America has over 800 military bases worldwide, and it is the only country that has that. Russia doesn't have that, China doesn't have that. Their home base is finished, but they have bases everywhere, and that is how they will successfully get China; then they return and see Babylon destroyed.

“Thy children shall they carry away captive, and, look, what thou hast, they shall spoil it, and mar the beauty of thy face.” Those are prisoners of war. It is the same as Jeremiah, where the mighty men’s hearts in Moab are “as the heart of a woman in her pangs”, very fearful, scared and afraid: “thy sons are taken captives, and thy daughters captives.” Whatever China says in its pride, God says it shall not be so. Nobody gets away with what they did to God's chosen people.

precepts.text: I will liken my judgment unto a ring: like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first. A steady flow of judgment comes upon all nations. So are we promoting harm to the Chinese? No. Some of you work for them and go to school with them; fine. Our job is to tell you what God says is going to happen to these nations, not just the Chinese, but all nations.
precepts.point: Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, saith the Lord. Although it happened with Nebuchadnezzar, God said it is going to happen again in the latter days. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
Jeremiah ends the judgment of Moab with “Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, saith the Lord. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.” Although it happened with Nebuchadnezzar, God said it is going to happen again in the latter days. Ezra shows how God's judgment runs: “I will liken my judgment unto a ring: like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.”

There is no slackness of the last plagues and judgments, and no swiftness of the first. It is a steady flow, a steady flow of judgment upon all nations. What came on Moab in the days of Nebuchadnezzar comes round again on Moab today, and the fear, the pit and the snare will find them even in the hidden bunker city under Beijing.

So are we promoting harm to the Chinese? No. Some of you work for them, some of you go to school with them. Fine, that's fine. Our job is to tell you what God says is going to happen to these nations: not just the Chinese, but all nations. The judgment is God's, it comes in its time, and it comes on every nation.

precepts.text: Moab is my washpot; the Most High set them beneath Israel as a servant.
precepts.point: The wickedness of Moab against the children of God is real history the American Board of Education does not teach: enslaving us during the Tang Dynasty, feeding the ghettos, and building whole industries off our people. All of it will be manifested and answered for.
precepts.why:
Moab is exceeding proud, with his loftiness, his arrogancy, his pride and the haughtiness of his heart. David shows where the Most High set Moab: “Moab is my washpot; over Edom will I cast out my shoe: Philistia, triumph thou because of me.”

Moab is his washpot; the Most High set them beneath Israel as a servant. For all that pride, these Moabites will go back to their proper place and serve the nation of Israel for what they have done. The wickedness of Moab against the children of God is real history the American Board of Education does not teach: enslaving us during the Tang Dynasty, feeding the ghettos, and building whole industries off our people. All of it will be manifested and answered for.

precepts.text: The house of Israel shall possess the nations for servants and handmaids in the land of the Lord.
precepts.point: The wickedness of Moab against the children of God is real history the American Board of Education does not teach: enslaving us during the Tang Dynasty, feeding the ghettos, and building whole industries off our people. All of it will be manifested and answered for.
precepts.why:
The Lord knows Moab's wrath, “but it shall not be so; his lies shall not so effect it.” Isaiah shows how it ends for the proud nations: “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.”

The house of Israel shall possess the nations for servants and handmaids in the land of the Lord. Moab, that enslaved us and built whole industries off our people, will be brought to his place and possessed by the children of God he oppressed; they shall take them captives whose captives they were, and rule over their oppressors.

points: Against Moab thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel. Unless you search the scriptures and pray to the Lord, you read that and say, I do not know who Moab is, and move on to the next chapter.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: We have heard the pride of Moab, (he is exceeding proud) his loftiness, and his arrogancy, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart. If you did not know the Chinese man was proud, you learned it these last few weeks.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: There shall be no more praise of Moab. You know how black people praise Moab: everybody was kung fu fighting; we love those Chinese movies. We will praise Moab quick, but Moab does not have that same love for us. Even today people say the next world superpower is going to be China; the prophecy says there shall be no more praise of Moab.
Also thou shalt be cut down, O Madmen. See what God calls Moab: madmen. That is the class title. When you read the history of Moab, they hated and despised our people; I will show you that.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: For because thou hast trusted in thy works and in thy treasures, thou shalt also be taken: captivity, prisoners of war. And Chemosh shall go forth into captivity with his priests and his princes together. Chemosh was the favorite idol god of Moab.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: The spoiler shall come upon every city, and no city shall escape. Nebuchadnezzar destroyed Moab then; Jeremiah's prophecy carries the duality, because Moab today, China, is a world superpower, and they will be destroyed once again. This goes with 2 Esdras 15:46-63 on the destruction of Asia and Babylon.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: Give wings unto Moab, that it may flee and get away. When Nebuchadnezzar came through, a lot of them fled far east. Some got caught; some did not.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: For was not Israel a derision unto thee? Since thou spakest of him, thou skippedst for joy. Why were they skipping for joy? Because Moab helped destroy us, and they were happy about it.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: Moab hath been at ease from his youth, and he hath settled on his lees, and hath not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither hath he gone into captivity. Vessel to vessel means taken captive and brought from one slavery to the next, like we were. That did not happen to Moab: therefore his taste remained in him, and his scent is not changed. Their hatred has not changed from their beginning until now.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel their confidence.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: The calamity of Moab is near to come, and his affliction hasteth fast. How is the strong staff broken, and the beautiful rod! Dibon, Aroer, Arnon: cities of ancient Moab, in the land America calls Jordan today.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: Make ye him drunken: for he magnified himself against the Lord. Notice why God says make Moab drunk: that is what they did to us. Moab also shall wallow in his vomit, and he also shall be in derision. For was not Israel a derision unto thee? You danced when you slaughtered us; you skipped for joy when we fell. So now they are going to get judged the same way.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: O ye that dwell in Moab, leave the cities, and dwell in the rock. Images shown in class: China's bunkers in the mountains, little bunkers, big bunkers, all kinds of bunkers. The prophecy already saw it.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: I know his wrath, saith the Lord; but it shall not be so; his lies shall not so effect it. Video played in class: a Chinese commentator boasting that China will not fire the first shot but will never allow a second, describing an ICBM carrying dozens of warheads that can reach any corner of the world in under twenty minutes, and promising that whoever wants to destroy China will be destroyed. Now that is some pride right there. Whatever China says, God says it shall not be so: his lies will not affect the outcome of what God says is going to happen to him.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: I will cause to cease in Moab, saith the Lord, him that offereth in the high places, and him that burneth incense to his gods. Video played in class: the incense counts of Chinese devotion, 108 sticks to the Buddhas, 32 to the devas of the four directions, 21 praying to one's father, sticks for every deity and ancestor. China is known for burning incense to its gods; more proof of who Moab is.

points: Every head shall be bald, and every beard clipped: the mourning of Moab returns. For I have broken Moab like a vessel wherein is no pleasure, saith the Lord.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: Fear, and the pit, and the snare, shall be upon thee, O inhabitant of Moab. He that fleeth from the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that getteth up out of the pit shall be taken in the snare. Article shown in class: the hidden metropolis, the Dixia Cheng, a sprawling cold war bunker city beneath Beijing. They think they will be safe in these underground bunkers; the Lord is telling us in the scripture that it is not going to work.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: This is the word of the Most High against Moab. Woe unto Nebo, for it is spoiled; Kiriathaim is confounded and taken. There shall be no more praise of Moab.
In Heshbon they have devised evil against it: come, let us cut it off from being a nation. These are the Moabites, and God calls the so-called Chinese by that name.
A voice of crying goes up from Horonaim, spoiling and great destruction. Moab is destroyed, and her little ones cause a cry to be heard.
Flee, save your lives, and be like the heath in the wilderness. There is no standing against the judgment that is coming.
Because thou hast trusted in thy works and in thy treasures, thou shalt also be taken. Chemosh their god goes into captivity with his priests and princes together.
The spoiler comes upon every city, and no city escapes. The valley perishes and the plain is destroyed, as the Most High has spoken.
Cursed be he that doeth the work of the Lord deceitfully, and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood. The work of the Most High is not to be done half-heartedly.
Moab has been at ease from his youth and settled on his lees, never emptied from vessel to vessel, never gone into captivity. Therefore his taste remained in him and his scent is not changed.
The Most High will send wanderers to empty his vessels and break their bottles, and Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel.
How say ye, we are mighty and strong men for the war? Moab is spoiled, and his chosen young men are gone down to the slaughter, saith the King, whose name is the Lord of hosts.
The calamity of Moab is near to come and his affliction hastens fast. All that know his name are to bemoan how the strong staff is broken.

The daughter that inhabits Dibon is told to come down from her glory and sit in thirst, for the spoiler of Moab comes upon her. The inhabitant of Aroer is to stand by the way and ask the one who flees, what is done.
Moab is confounded, for it is broken down. Howl and cry, and tell it in Arnon that Moab is spoiled.
Judgment comes on the whole plain country, city by city, from Holon and Jahazah to Dibon, Nebo, Kiriathaim, Kerioth, and Bozrah, upon all the cities of Moab, far or near.
The horn of Moab is cut off and her arm is broken. The strength of the nation is taken away by the Most High.
Make Moab drunken, for he magnified himself against the Lord, and he shall wallow in his own vomit and be in derision.

The Most High asks, was not Israel a derision unto thee? Did the Lord not punish his own children? Then what makes the heathen think their time is not going to come? He punishes his own, so he will surely punish the wicked.

The pride of Moab is called out: exceedingly proud, his loftiness, his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his heart. For all that pride, these Moabites will go back to their proper place and serve the nation of Israel for what they have done.

The Most High declares he will howl and mourn for Moab, for the men of Kir-heres and the vine of Sibmah, because the spoiler is fallen upon the summer fruits and the vintage. Joy and gladness is taken from the plentiful field.
He will cause to cease in Moab him that offereth in the high places and him that burneth incense to his gods. The idolatry is cut off with the people.

The heart of the Most High sounds like pipes for Moab, because the riches he has gotten are perished. Every head shall be bald and every beard clipped, with cutting upon the hands and sackcloth upon the loins.

A good majority of Moab bald their heads and shave their faces rather than keep their beards, the same as the Mongolians right next door to them. There shall be lamenting generally upon the housetops of Moab.
Moab is broken like a vessel wherein is no pleasure. They howl, asking how it is broken down, and Moab becomes a derision and a dismay to all around him.

He that judges shall fly as an eagle and spread his wings over Moab. The mighty men's hearts that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pains, and Moab shall be destroyed from being a people because he magnified himself against the Lord.

Fear, the pit, and the snare are upon the inhabitants of Moab. He that flees the fear falls into the pit, and he that climbs out of the pit is taken in the snare; there is no escape from the years of their visitation.
A fire comes forth out of Heshbon and devours the corner of Moab. Woe unto Moab, for thy sons and thy daughters are taken captives.

Yet the Most High will bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days. This has not happened yet, but it will come to pass, for he has spoken it and his word shall not return. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.
